name: Midnight-Monolith
specific_features: The Monolith emits faint electromagnetic pulses at irregular intervals
description: Midnight-Monolith is a cold, dark rocky world orbiting far from its star, its surface perpetually shrouded in deep twilight. Its defining feature is a single basalt formation spanning over four hundred kilometers, rising from the surface like a wall built by titans, its dark face absorbing what little light reaches this distant orbit.

The thin atmosphere carries fine dust that settles on everything, coating the landscape in a matte grey film. The silence is oppressive, broken only by the occasional crack of thermal contraction in the rock as the planet rotates its meager warmth away from the star.

The Monolith emits faint electromagnetic pulses at irregular intervals, a phenomenon that has resisted every attempt at explanation. The pulses contain no discernible pattern or information content, yet they have been recorded continuously for over a century of observation, never repeating the same interval twice.

The planet's mineral resources are unremarkable, but the Monolith draws a steady stream of researchers and signal theorists. Some believe the pulses are a form of communication from within the structure, while others argue they are a natural piezoelectric phenomenon on an unprecedented scale.
